messages.author: 1c8b9e31e3450098
messages.subject: symbolic regression
parts:
I've been going over the emails concerning the objections to symbolic
regression, and I have three questions:

1. Do you think it is possible to construct a symbolic regression
proposal which would be appropriate for R?

It seems unlikely to me that the idea of symbolic regression can't be
rescued by measuring goodness of fit carefully, and that doing so is a
worthy endeavor to advance statistics in its own right. 2. Is there
any evidence to the contrary?

3. Why is http://rwiki.sciviews.org/doku.php?id=developers:projects:gsoc2010:syrfr
displaying in raw, unformatted wikitext?

Regards,
James Salsman

messages.author: ec32e5a92a275a89
messages.subject: Re: symbolic regression
parts:
Though I was instigator and mentor for radx project, my main interest in automatic vs
symbolic differentiation and other such tasks is to be able to generate gradients or
Jacobians when the function is not totally algebraic e.g., has IF() or other constructs. I
don't know enough yet to comment on feasibility. Nor can I comment on the wiki issue.

For me there is no objection to symbolic math tools for R. Quite the contrary.

One concern that affects all packages is that they should "work together" so that where
either will do the task, the user only needs a single calling style, with some sort of
parameter "method = 'symbolic'" etc. I'd be unhappy if there were great differences.
Indeed, in building optimx, Ravi and I had to leave out one or two methods because the
calling sequences were just too awkward. This is a general issue, but one that I believe
is very important to users, and I know from experience takes work and cooperation from
developers.

Best,

John Nash
